title: Integral normalization of coefficient perturbations at a simple root
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $v:F\to\Gamma\cup\{\infty\}$ an additive valuation and $\mathcal O$ its valuation subring [def-trf-valuation-ring], with maximal ideal and residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Give $F$ a nondiscrete topology with neighbourhood basis $\{y:v(y-x)>\gamma\}$ for every $x$, indexed by every finite ambient value $\gamma$. Let $f=X^n+\sum_{i<n}c_iX^i$, $n\ge1$, with $f(a)=0$ and $f^{\prime}(a)\ne0$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. For every open neighbourhood $U$ of $a$, there are an open neighbourhood $V$ of $c$ in $F^n$ and fixed nonzero $s,t\in F$ such that $a+s\mathfrak m_{\mathcal O}\subset U$ and, for every $d\in V$, there is $H_d\in\mathcal O[X]$ with $\overline H_d=X$ and $g_d(a+sX)=tH_d(X)$ after mapping coefficients into $F$, where $g_d=X^n+\sum_{i<n}d_iX^i$. Henselianity, completeness, rank one, and root existence for $g_d$ are not assumed or asserted.

proof.text: From the neighbourhood basis choose a finite gamma whose ball about a lies in U. Put lambda=f prime(a), which is nonzero. Write f(a+Z)=lambda Z+sum for j>=2 of A_j Z^j; the constant and linear terms follow by evaluation and formal differentiation.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, root-perturbation form of Krasner used in the cited Bourbaki VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), part (2), is the simple-root input, not itself this topological conclusion.

proof.text: Every zero-centred finite-radius ball contains a nonzero element: if one did not, translating the same ball basis would make every singleton open and the topology discrete. Take a finite maximum of gamma, zero and v(lambda)-v(A_j) for the finitely many nonzero A_j with j>=2. Choose s nonzero with value exceeding this maximum.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, root-perturbation form of Krasner used in the cited Bourbaki VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), part (2), is the simple-root input, not itself this topological conclusion.

proof.text: For each j>=2 with A_j nonzero, v(A_j*s^(j-1)/lambda)=(v(A_j)+v(s)-v(lambda))+(j-2)*v(s)>0. Zero A_j automatically satisfy the required coefficient condition. Let t=lambda*s; then s and t are nonzero.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, root-perturbation form of Krasner used in the cited Bourbaki VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), part (2), is the simple-root input, not itself this topological conclusion.

proof.text: For g=X^n+sum(d_i X^i), write g(a+Z)-f(a+Z)=sum(E_j Z^j). The binomial expansion gives E_j=sum over j<=i<n of (d_i-c_i)*binom(i,j)*a^(i-j); E_n=0. Put t_j=v(lambda)+(1-j)*v(s). Choose eta at least the finitely many finite t_j-v(binom(i,j)*a^(i-j)) for nonzero multipliers. If all v(d_i-c_i)>eta, every summand of E_j has value greater than t_j, hence v(E_j)>t_j by the valuation inequality for finite sums.

proof.text: Strict balls are open: if v(x-c)>eta, the ball v(y-x)>eta is contained in it by the ultrametric inequality, and this ball is a neighbourhood by the given basis. Their finite product V is open and contains c.

proof.text: For d in V form the explicit field polynomial g(a+sX)/t. Its constant coefficient E_0/(lambda*s) has positive value, its linear coefficient 1+E_1/lambda is congruent to 1, and for j>=2 its coefficient (A_j+E_j)*s^(j-1)/lambda has positive value by the preceding bounds. Thus these coefficients belong to the valuation subring O [def-trf-valuation-ring]. Lift the polynomial coefficientwise to O[X]; its image times C(t) is exactly g.comp(C(a)+C(s)*X).

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.374, root-perturbation form of Krasner used in the cited Bourbaki VI section 8 exercises 12 and 14(a). Stacks algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), part (2), is the simple-root input, not itself this topological conclusion.

proof.text: In a valuation subring, an element of nonnegative value is a unit exactly when its value is zero, since its inverse has the opposite value. Thus its maximal ideal is exactly the elements of positive value. The coefficient bounds give Hbar=X. For z in the maximal ideal, v(s*z)>gamma, so a+s*z belongs to U. This includes z=0; for n=1 there are no higher coefficients and E_n=0.

theorem exists_open_coefficients_residue_X
    (F : Type u) [Field F] (Γ : Type v) [LinearOrderedAddCommGroupWithTop Γ]
    (v : AddValuation F Γ) [TopologicalSpace F]
    (hvaltop : ∀ x : F, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (fun γ : Γ ↦ γ ≠ ⊤)
      (fun γ ↦ {y : F | γ < v (y - x)}))
    (hnd : ¬ DiscreteTopology F)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (c : Fin n → F) (a : F)
    (ha : (X ^ n + ∑ i : Fin n, C (c i) * X ^ (i : ℕ)).IsRoot a)
    (hda : (X ^ n + ∑ i : Fin n, C (c i) * X ^ (i : ℕ)).derivative.eval a ≠ 0)
    (U : Set F) (hU : IsOpen U) (haU : a ∈ U) :
    ∃ V : Set (Fin n → F), IsOpen V ∧ c ∈ V ∧
      ∃ s t : F, s ≠ 0 ∧ t ≠ 0 ∧
        (∀ z : v.toValuation.valuationSubring,
          z ∈ maximalIdeal v.toValuation.valuationSubring → a + s * (z : F) ∈ U) ∧
        ∀ d : Fin n → F, d ∈ V →
          ∃ H : Polynomial v.toValuation.valuationSubring,
            H.map (residue v.toValuation.valuationSubring) = X ∧
            (X ^ n + ∑ i : Fin n, C (d i) * X ^ (i : ℕ)).comp (C a + C s * X) =
              C t * H.map v.toValuation.valuationSubring.subtype
